title: Backpressure triggers, hysteresis windows and safeguard relays for routing
creator: Aisha Gomez
description:
Problem: During sudden regional load spikes and dependent service errors (429s/timeout/5xx), customer routes observe cascading retries and oscillation between model variants. We need an automated defensive layer that detects overloaded signals, applies graded backpressure, and flips to safe model variants or regional handovers while avoiding thrash.

Goal: Implement a set of automatic fallback triggers combined with stateful circuit-breaker relays and hysteresis windows that: 1) classify overload signals (client 429s, internal timeouts, elevated error rates), 2) decide graded mitigations (rate reduction, route-level concurrency caps, model-variant fallback, regional handover), and 3) provide observability and manual override hooks in the Console and API. The system should be deterministic, low-latency, and reversible with safe cooldowns.
acceptance_criteria: Signal classification implemented: 429 burst detector, p99 latency anomaly, and rolling error-rate windows (30s, 5m)
Three-tier mitigation strategy implemented: soft-shed (throttling), variant-fallback (quantized model), handover (regional re-route)
Circuit-relay state machine with hysteresis to prevent flip-flop; cooldown and progressive recovery paths documented and implemented
Telemetry surfaced to Console: per-route trip reason, trip duration, current mitigation level, and recent signal metrics
E2E test harness validates triggers for synthetic 429 spikes, induced timeouts, and steady-state error-rate regressions
Runbook updated and a rollout plan that can rollback via feature-flag within 15 minutes
design_notes: Use probabilistic dampening: require sustained threshold breach across two consecutive windows to avoid reactive flips for bursts
Hysteresis windows: enter threshold at 30s sliding window; require 3x window without breach to clear (configurable per-route)
Mitigation levels: L1=rate cap (soft-shed 10-30%), L2=variant fallback to compatible quantized model, L3=regional handover to secondary AZ/region or reserved capacity pool
State machine: CLOSED -> PROBING -> OPEN (L1) -> OPEN (L2) -> OPEN (L3) -> RECOVERING -> CLOSED
Signal fusion: combine client 429 rate with internal 5xx percent and p99 latency z-score to compute a single overload score
Expose per-customer overrides and whitelist lists to skip fallback for critical customers (shown in Console RBAC)
engineering_notes: Runtime hook points: router pre-eval (before model selection) and post-eval (on error) to update sliding windows
Storage: use Redis for lightweight ephemeral trip states with TTLs; persist incidents to timeseries for observability (Prometheus + Loki traces)
Rate limiting interplay: integrate with existing quota layer; soft-shed implemented as a token-bucket multiplier applied to route concurrency tokens
Fallback compatibility matrix required: ensure model variant offers same API/response schema or transform layer present
Graceful KV-cache warming: when switching to a variant, warm KV cache using sampled queries to avoid cold latency spikes
Memory/CPU safety: circuit evaluation should be bounded CPU work per request (sampling + aggregated counters) to avoid adding overhead under load
implementation_tasks: ENG-87212: instrumentation - sliding-window counters and z-score compute (Marcus)
ENG-87213: state machine library and Redis-backed relay store (backend infra)
ENG-87214: router changes - mitigation enforcement hooks and variant selection (runtime team)
ENG-87215: console - UI for manual override, view trip logs, and config per-route (frontend)
ENG-87216: e2e tests and chaos harness to inject 429s/timeouts (SRE)
ENG-87217: rollout via feature-flag + canary to 5% routes then 50% then global (release)
ENG-87218: postmortem automation to capture trip context for future incidents
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Feature branch + unit tests + design review (1 week)
Stage 1: Deploy to staging with synthetic traffic profiles; validate metrics and Console surfaces (3 days)
Stage 2: Canary to low-risk routes (5% traffic) for 48 hours; monitor false-positive trips
Stage 3: Progressive ramp to 50% over 72 hours if SLOs stable
Stage 4: Full rollout with alerting thresholds and runbook in place
Rollback: kill feature-flag or set global disable; state store TTL expires and routes return to CLOSED
test_plan: Unit tests for window math, hysteresis clearing, and state transitions
Integration tests validating end-to-end enforcement (throttling => lower accepted rate)
Chaos tests: inject 429 flood from simulated clients; verify L1 then escalate to L2/L3 according to thresholds
Performance tests: ensure circuit evaluation adds <100us median overhead per request at 99th percentile
Security review: ensure no sensitive data logged to trips; KMS policy for persisted incidents
metrics: Primary: trip_rate (trips/minute) by route and region
Primary: average mitigation_level and mean duration per trip
SLOs: end-to-end p95 latency and error_rate before/after mitigation
Operational: false_positive_rate (trips triggered with no upstream issues) < 2%
Capacity: number of regional handovers per week (aim < 5 for steady-state)
dependencies: ENG-82222 (variant compatibility matrix and model metadata API)
